# Architecture Document for Disability-Claim-SponsorConnect

## Overview
The Disability-Claim-SponsorConnect application is designed to facilitate guided online submission of disability claims specifically for plan sponsors via the SponsorConnect platform.

## Stack
This application is developed using the following technology stack:
- **Programming Language**: Java 21
- **Framework**: Spring Boot 3.3
- **Build**: Maven; tests run under JUnit 5 with JaCoCo line coverage

## Current Scope
- All seven components are implemented: `claim-identification` (US-1), `data-prepopulation` (US-2), `claim-details-collection` (US-3), `document-upload` (US-4), `submission-confirmation` (US-5), `submission-status` (US-6) and `packetization` (US-7).
- There is no database and no intake system. Plan and member data are in-memory synthetic catalogues; claim journeys, their documents, their confirmations and their intake deliveries are held in memory; and the intake gateway records what it is handed rather than sending it anywhere. Every one of those is a stand-in behind a port, and each is named below.

## Architecture Components

### claim-identification (US-1, Portal Team)
Package `com.maplesure.sponsorconnect.claimidentification`.

| Type | Role |
|---|---|
| `ClaimIdentificationController` (`web`) | HTTP edge for `POST /api/claims/identification`; maps outcomes to status codes and gates on the feature flag |
| `ClaimIdentificationService` | Validates the submitted identifiers, then resolves them through the directory |
| `MemberPlanDirectory` | Lookup port — the seam where US-2's pre-population interface replaces the local implementation |
| `InMemoryMemberPlanDirectory` | Directory backed by a fixed record set, matched case-insensitively |
| `SyntheticMemberPlanCatalogue` | The synthetic records seeded into that directory |
| `ClaimIdentificationFeature` | Binds the `enableClaimIdentification` flag from `features.enable-claim-identification` |

Validation lives in the service rather than as bean-validation annotations on the request body, so the rules are covered by plain unit tests and apply to every caller, not only the HTTP edge. Format errors are reported for all fields at once; a directory lookup only happens once both values are well-formed.

### data-prepopulation (US-2, Services Team)
Package `com.maplesure.sponsorconnect.dataprepopulation`.

| Type | Role |
|---|---|
| `DataPrepopulationController` (`web`) | HTTP edge for `POST /api/claims/prepopulation` and `/review`; gates on the feature flag |
| `DataPrepopulationService` | Identifies via US-1, builds the form, validates and applies corrections, confirms |
| `ClaimFormField` | The field catalogue and, per field, who owns it — sponsors may correct employment facts, not plan facts |
| `PrepopulatedClaimForm` / `FormField` | The form as reviewed, each field carrying its value, `FieldSource` and editability |
| `ConfirmedClaimDetails` | Flat confirmed values plus the list of fields the sponsor corrected |
| `MemberDetailsProvider` | Port for the details system of record |
| `SyntheticMemberDetailsProvider` | Synthetic stand-in for that source |
| `DataPrepopulationFeature` | Binds the `enableDataPrepopulation` flag |

Identification is delegated to US-1's `ClaimIdentificationService` rather than reimplemented, so the two steps cannot disagree on what a valid identifier is. The form is re-derived server-side on review rather than round-tripped through the client, so insurer-owned values cannot be altered in transit; only named corrections to editable fields are applied. Pre-population is best-effort — a member with nothing on file yields `MISSING` fields, not an error — but confirmation is refused while any editable field is still empty.

### claim-details-collection (US-3, Portal Team)
Package `com.maplesure.sponsorconnect.claimdetailscollection`.

| Type | Role |
|---|---|
| `ClaimDetailsCollectionController` (`web`) | HTTP edge for `POST /api/claims/journey`, `/{id}/steps/{step}`, `/{id}/submit` and `GET /{id}`; gates on the feature flag |
| `ClaimDetailsCollectionService` | Opens the journey from confirmed details, records each step, submits the claim |
| `ClaimJourneyStep` / `ClaimDetailField` | The step and field catalogue — what is asked, in what order, and what counts as an answer |
| `StepValidator` | Checks one step: field ownership, value format, and the dates that have to agree with each other |
| `ClaimJourney` | One sponsor's progress — confirmed details, collected answers, status, and the guidance derived from them |
| `ClaimJourneyRepository` | Port for the claim store |
| `InMemoryClaimJourneyRepository` | Journey store held in memory until a datastore exists |
| `ClaimJourneyResponse` (`web`) | The journey as the guided form renders it, guidance included |
| `ClaimDetailsCollectionFeature` | Binds the `enableGuidedClaimJourney` flag |

The journey collects only claim facts the sponsor is the authority on; everything already held about the member and plan arrives as US-2's `ConfirmedClaimDetails` and is not re-asked. Starting the journey *is* the confirmation of the pre-populated details, so the sponsor's corrections and their confirmation cannot be separated by a lost call. The step, not the field, is the unit of progress: a step submission is validated whole and recorded whole, so no journey holds half a step. Re-answering a recorded step replaces it — and re-checks the dates against what is already stored, so a corrected last day worked cannot leave an absence starting before it.

### document-upload (US-4, Portal Team)
Package `com.maplesure.sponsorconnect.documentupload`.

| Type | Role |
|---|---|
| `DocumentUploadController` (`web`) | HTTP edge for `POST` and `GET /api/claims/journey/{journeyId}/documents`; accepts `multipart/form-data` parts named `files`; gates on the feature flag |
| `DocumentUploadService` | Resolves the claim through US-3, applies the policy, stores the upload |
| `DocumentPolicy` | The file type and size rules, as a value rather than constants |
| `UploadedDocument` / `ClaimDocument` | A document as sent, and as stored against a claim |
| `ClaimDocumentRepository` | Port for the document store |
| `InMemoryClaimDocumentRepository` | Document store held in memory until a real one exists |
| `DocumentUploadResponse` / `ClaimDocumentResponse` (`web`) | The claim's attachments — reference, name, type and size, never content |
| `DocumentUploadFeature` | Binds the `enableDocumentUpload` flag |

An upload is accepted whole or not at all, for the same reason a journey step is: attaching related documents is one act, and leaving a sponsor to work out which half of it landed would be worse than asking for the set again. Every failing file is reported at once, one fault per file — the first thing wrong with it is the thing they have to fix.

A document is identified in an error by its **position in the upload**, never by its file name: the name is a sponsor-supplied value, and this component holds to the same rule as the rest — supplied values are not echoed back, in messages or in logs. The type check is on what the browser declared; reading the leading bytes to confirm it belongs with the virus scan and the real document store, not here.

### submission-confirmation (US-5, Portal Team)
Package `com.maplesure.sponsorconnect.submissionconfirmation`.

| Type | Role |
|---|---|
| `SubmissionConfirmationController` (`web`) | HTTP edge for `POST`, `GET` and `GET /download` on `/api/claims/journey/{journeyId}/confirmation`; gates on the feature flag |
| `SubmissionConfirmationService` | Issues the confirmation for a submitted claim, once, and serves it thereafter |
| `SubmissionConfirmation` | Reference number, the claim it belongs to, when it was submitted, how many documents went with it |
| `ReferenceNumberGenerator` / `RandomReferenceNumberGenerator` | Port for what a reference looks like, and the shipped form of it |
| `SubmissionConfirmationRepository` | Port for the confirmation store |
| `InMemorySubmissionConfirmationRepository` | Confirmation store held in memory until a real one exists |
| `ConfirmationReceipt` (`web`) | The confirmation rendered as a plain-text file to keep |
| `SubmissionConfirmationFeature` | Binds the `enableSubmissionConfirmation` flag |

A reference number is issued once per claim and never reissued — that is the whole point of it. Idempotence is enforced at the store with `putIfAbsent` rather than by a read-then-write in the service, because two requests confirming the same claim at once must not leave a sponsor holding two numbers for one claim, and only the map can settle that race.

The reference alphabet omits `0`, `1`, `I`, `L` and `O`, and groups characters in fours: a sponsor reads this number down a telephone, and those are the characters they get wrong. It is drawn from a `SecureRandom` so references cannot be walked through — a reference is quoted as proof a claim was submitted.

The submission time comes from an injected `Clock` rather than `Instant.now()` at the call site, so it can be pinned in a test instead of being whatever the clock said while the suite ran. The response renders it as an ISO-8601 string rather than leaving an `Instant` for Jackson to interpret: how a date leaves this service is part of its contract, not something that should shift with a mapper's configuration.

### submission-status (US-6, Services Team)
Package `com.maplesure.sponsorconnect.submissionstatus`.

| Type | Role |
|---|---|
| `SubmissionStatusController` (`web`) | HTTP edge for `GET /api/claims/journey/{journeyId}/status`; gates on the feature flag |
| `SubmissionStatusService` | Derives the view from the claim, its documents and its confirmation |
| `SubmissionStage` | How far the claim has got — outstanding, ready, submitted, confirmed |
| `OutstandingItem` | One thing the sponsor still has to do |
| `SubmissionStatus` | The view itself, and the response shape |
| `SubmissionStatusFeature` | Binds the `enableSubmissionStatus` flag |

**This component stores nothing, and that is the design.** There is no status field anywhere in the codebase and no repository in this package — the view is derived on every request from the components that own the facts. A status that is written down is a status that can disagree with the thing it describes; the accuracy US-6-AC2 asks for is far easier to guarantee than to maintain. It is also the only component here with no port to a system of record, because it has no facts of its own.

`SubmissionStatus` is returned to the client directly rather than through a separate response record, as the other components do. It is already a presentation view rather than a domain type — it exists only to be looked at — so a second type between it and the wire would carry no decisions.

Outstanding items list the whole remaining path, not only the next step: a sponsor returning to a half-finished claim is deciding whether they have time to finish it. Only genuine blockers appear — a claim with no documents is not outstanding, because nothing else in the service requires one, and a status view must not invent obligations the process does not enforce.

Two limitations are worth stating rather than discovering. Status is addressed by claim reference alone: no store offers a query by policy or member, so a "my claims" listing needs a real datastore behind the existing seams, not another endpoint. And a claim reports no submission time until it is confirmed, because the time is recorded when the reference is issued (US-5) and the journey itself keeps none.

### packetization (US-7, Intake Integration Team)
Package `com.maplesure.sponsorconnect.packetization`.

| Type | Role |
|---|---|
| `PacketizationController` (`web`) | HTTP edge for `GET /packet`, `POST /packet/send` and `GET /packet/delivery`; gates on the feature flag |
| `PacketizationService` | Assembles the packet, and hands it across once |
| `ClaimPacket` / `PacketDocument` | The claim as one unit: details, documents with content, digests |
| `PacketDigest` | SHA-256 over a document, and over a packet's content |
| `IntakeGateway` | The **outbound** port — the boundary a packet crosses |
| `RecordingIntakeGateway` | Stand-in for intake: takes a packet, acknowledges it, keeps it |
| `IntakeDeliveryLedger` / `InMemoryIntakeDeliveryLedger` | The record of what has been sent, and the guard against sending twice |
| `PacketManifestResponse` (`web`) | A packet described — never its documents' content |
| `PacketizationFeature` | Binds the `enablePacketization` flag |

A packet is assembled whole, digested whole, and delivered in **one** call. Intake correlating a claim's information with its documents from separate messages is the failure this component exists to remove, so the association is not left to a shared identifier in two messages.

The packet digest covers the claim reference, the details sorted by field name, and the documents' own digests in packet order — but never the packet id. The same claim therefore always digests the same way, which is what makes the digest worth anything: intake can compare what arrived against what it was told to expect, and a resend is recognisably the same packet rather than a second claim.

**Exactly-once is the ledger's job, not the caller's.** `IntakeDeliveryLedger.deliverOnce` runs the delivery inside itself rather than being consulted before one. A check-then-send-then-record in the service would read correctly and lose the race: two requests could both find no record and intake would file the claim twice. `InMemoryIntakeDeliveryLedger` uses `computeIfAbsent`, which holds the entry while the delivery runs — a heavier thing to do inside a map than one would normally choose, and the honest cost of exactly-once against an in-memory store. With a real store this becomes a unique constraint on the claim plus an idempotency key on the intake call. A delivery that throws records nothing, so a claim intake could not take can be sent again.

There is no intake system to talk to. Rather than invent a protocol nobody has agreed, or leave the boundary undefined until there is one, the shipped adapter records what crossed it — so what a real adapter will have to carry is written down and tested rather than assumed. When intake exists, `intakeGateway()` is the single bean that changes and nothing above it moves.

Sending is a deliberate action on this component's endpoint rather than something that fires when a sponsor confirms. Firing it automatically would mean changing `submission-confirmation`, which belongs to another team; that is a follow-up ticket, not a wider diff.

## Data Management
- No datastore. The plan and member catalogues are in memory and synthetic: invented policy numbers, member ids, plan labels, coverage statuses and member details. Nothing here is client-identifiable, in code, configuration or tests. Journeys, their uploaded documents, their issued confirmations and their intake deliveries are in memory too and do not survive a restart — whole files sit on the heap, and a reference number that does not outlive a restart is the plainest statement that these stores are stand-ins. The delivery ledger is the one where that matters most: a ledger that forgets on restart would let a claim reach intake twice.
- Submitted identifiers, field values and file names are never written to logs and are never echoed back in error messages. Rejections are logged by error code only; correction and answer errors name the field, upload errors name the position, and neither names a value. Reference numbers are not logged either, and neither is anything from inside a packet.
- Document content leaves this service in exactly one direction: inside a packet, to intake. It is never rendered back over HTTP — the upload listing and the packet manifest both describe documents by name, type, size and digest.

## Integration Boundaries
The steps chain in-process, each consuming the one before it rather than reimplementing it: `DataPrepopulationService` consumes `ClaimIdentificationService` and its `IdentifiedMemberPlan`; `ClaimDetailsCollectionService` consumes `DataPrepopulationService` and its `ConfirmedClaimDetails`; `DocumentUploadService` consumes `ClaimDetailsCollectionService` to resolve the claim its documents belong to; `SubmissionConfirmationService` consumes both of those — the journey for the claim's identity and submitted state, the document component for what went with it; `SubmissionStatusService` consumes all three, reading each fact from the component that owns it; and `PacketizationService` consumes the same three to assemble what intake receives. Each component keeps its own port to its system of record — `MemberPlanDirectory` for plan and member lookup, `MemberDetailsProvider` for held details, `ClaimJourneyRepository` for the claim store, `ClaimDocumentRepository` for the document store, `SubmissionConfirmationRepository` for issued confirmations, `IntakeDeliveryLedger` for what has been sent — so each can be swapped for a real adapter independently. `submission-status` has no such port, because it owns no facts.

`IntakeGateway` is the only **outbound** port in the application: every other one reads from a system of record, and this writes to another system. It is therefore the only boundary where a mistake reaches somebody else's data, which is why exactly-once delivery is enforced by the ledger rather than by discipline at the call site.

These in-process dependencies are on the concrete services, not on interfaces: the ports in this architecture face outward to systems of record, not sideways between components. That is a deliberate limit rather than an oversight — the components deploy as one application and share a release — but it is the reason a component's tests build the chain beneath it, and it is what would have to change first if any of these were ever to be split out.

## Feature Flags and Rollback
`enableClaimIdentification`, `enableDataPrepopulation`, `enableGuidedClaimJourney`, `enableDocumentUpload`, `enableSubmissionConfirmation`, `enableSubmissionStatus` and `enablePacketization` all default to off, so each endpoint is dark until a deployment enables it. Rollback is flipping the flag; removing the component code is the follow-up, per each story's rollback plan. The flags are independent: each component depends on the *services* it consumes, not their HTTP edges, so packetization functions with every sponsor-facing endpoint still dark.

Three carry a property that matters when planning a release:

- **`enableSubmissionConfirmation`** — references are issued once and stored, so turning it off and on again does not renumber a claim already confirmed.
- **`enableSubmissionStatus`** — nothing is stored, so turning it off leaves no residue at all.
- **`enablePacketization`** — with it off, nothing is packaged and nothing crosses the boundary; there is a test asserting intake hears nothing while it is dark. But rollback here is not symmetric: packets already delivered stay delivered. Flipping the flag off stops further sends, it does not recall what intake has taken. That is the one place in this application where a flag cannot undo what enabling it did, and it should be read before the flag is turned on rather than after.

> **Note:** This document will be updated as the application is developed and components are implemented.

# README for Disability-Claim-SponsorConnect

## Introduction
The Disability-Claim-SponsorConnect is an innovative solution aimed at providing plan sponsors a guided online platform for disability claim submissions, integrated within the SponsorConnect ecosystem.

## Features
- Plan sponsors will have a streamlined process for submitting disability claims.
- **Member and plan identification (US-1)** — a sponsor enters a policy number and member ID and the system identifies the plan and member the claim is for, or explains why it could not.
- **Data pre-population (US-2)** — the claim form is pre-filled with the details already held for that plan and member, and the sponsor can correct or confirm them.
- **Guided claim details collection (US-3)** — a step-by-step journey collects the employment and absence details the sponsor is the authority on, and stores them on submission.
- **Multiple document uploads (US-4)** — related supporting documents attach to the claim in one upload, within a stated file type and size policy.
- **Submission confirmation (US-5)** — a submitted claim gets a reference number the sponsor can copy or download, issued once and fixed thereafter.
- **Submission status (US-6)** — a sponsor returning to a claim sees where it stands and everything still outstanding, derived fresh on every request.
- **Intake packetization (US-7)** — a confirmed claim's information and documents are packaged as one digest-bound packet and handed to intake in a single delivery, once.

## Technology Stack
- The application is built using Java 21, leveraging the Spring Boot framework for a robust backend.
- Build and test with Maven.

## Current Status
- **All seven stories are delivered**: `claim-identification` (US-1), `data-prepopulation` (US-2), `claim-details-collection` (US-3), `document-upload` (US-4), `submission-confirmation` (US-5), `submission-status` (US-6) and `packetization` (US-7).
- Every one ships behind its own feature flag, all off by default. There is still no datastore and no intake system: the stores and the intake gateway are in-memory stand-ins behind ports, and the sections below say so where it matters.

## Installation
Requires JDK 21 and Maven.

```bash
mvn test          # run the test suite
mvn spring-boot:run
```

## Usage

### Identify a member and plan

`POST /api/claims/identification`

```json
{ "policyNumber": "P100234", "memberId": "M0004821" }
```

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | Plan and member identified; the body carries the plan and coverage details. |
| `400` | The policy number or member ID is missing or malformed. |
| `422` | Both values are well-formed, but no plan and member match them. |
| `404` | The `enableClaimIdentification` feature flag is off. |

Errors come back as a list so the guided form can mark every field at fault at once:

```json
{
  "errors": [
    { "field": "policyNumber", "code": "POLICY_NUMBER_INVALID",
      "message": "Policy number must be the letter P followed by 6 digits, for example P100234." }
  ]
}
```

Identifier formats (synthetic scheme): policy number `P` + 6 digits, member ID `M` + 7 digits. Matching is case-insensitive and surrounding whitespace is trimmed.

### Pre-populate the claim form

`POST /api/claims/prepopulation`

```json
{ "policyNumber": "P100234", "memberId": "M0004821" }
```

Returns the form with every field's value, where it came from (`PREPOPULATED`, `SPONSOR_CORRECTED`, `MISSING`) and whether the sponsor may edit it. Employment facts are editable; plan and coverage facts are shown read-only. A member with nothing on file is not an error — the fields come back `MISSING` for the sponsor to complete.

### Review: correct or confirm

`POST /api/claims/prepopulation/review`

```json
{
  "policyNumber": "P100234",
  "memberId": "M0004821",
  "corrections": { "occupation": "Warehouse Manager" },
  "confirm": true
}
```

`confirm: false` returns the corrected form so the sponsor can keep reviewing; `confirm: true` returns the flat confirmed details plus `correctedFields`, the record of what the sponsor changed rather than accepted. The form is re-derived server-side from the identifiers, so only the named corrections are applied and only to editable fields.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | The pre-populated form, or the confirmed details |
| `400` | Bad identifiers, or a correction that cannot be applied (unknown field, plan-owned field, blank value) |
| `422` | No plan and member match, or confirmation attempted with fields still empty |
| `404` | The `enableDataPrepopulation` feature flag is off |

### Collect the claim details

Starting a journey confirms the pre-populated details and opens the guided form. The steps then collect only what the sponsor is the authority on — nothing already held about the member or plan is asked again.

`POST /api/claims/journey`

```json
{ "policyNumber": "P100234", "memberId": "M0004821", "corrections": { "occupation": "Warehouse Manager" } }
```

The response is the journey: `currentStep`, `remainingSteps`, `missingFields`, `readyToSubmit`, the `confirmedDetails` carried from US-2 and the `collectedDetails` so far. Drive it with:

| Endpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/claims/journey/{journeyId}/steps/{step}` | Answer one step; the body is a flat map of field name to value |
| `GET /api/claims/journey/{journeyId}` | Read the journey back — how a sponsor resumes, and how a caller checks what was stored |
| `POST /api/claims/journey/{journeyId}/submit` | Store the collected details |

| Step | Fields |
|---|---|
| `employment` | `lastDayWorked` (date), `regularHoursPerWeek` (0 < hours ≤ 168), `salaryContinued` (`YES`/`NO`) |
| `absence` | `firstDayAbsent` (date), `absenceReason`, `expectedReturnDate` (date, optional) |

Dates are ISO `yyyy-MM-dd`. `firstDayAbsent` may not precede `lastDayWorked`, and `expectedReturnDate` may not precede `firstDayAbsent`. A step is recorded whole or not at all: submit it half-answered and every outstanding field comes back at once, with nothing kept. Re-answering a step replaces it — going back to change an answer is part of the journey. Submission is refused while anything required is still empty, and a submitted claim no longer accepts changes.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | The journey, with the step to show next |
| `400` | An unknown step, or an answer that cannot be recorded |
| `422` | No plan and member match, details not yet confirmable, or the claim already submitted |
| `404` | No such journey, or the `enableGuidedClaimJourney` feature flag is off |

### Attach supporting documents

Related documents attach to a claim in one upload, as `multipart/form-data` with one or more parts named `files`.

`POST /api/claims/journey/{journeyId}/documents`

```bash
curl -F files=@claim-form.pdf -F files=@physician-statement.pdf \
     http://localhost:8080/api/claims/journey/$JOURNEY_ID/documents
```

`GET /api/claims/journey/{journeyId}/documents` lists what the claim carries. Both return the file name, declared type, size and reference of every document — never its content.

**File type and size policy** (`DocumentPolicy.standard()`):

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Accepted types | `application/pdf`, `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/tiff` |
| Largest document | 10 MB |
| Documents per claim | 20 |

An upload is accepted whole or not at all: attaching related documents is one act, so if any file breaks the policy nothing is stored and every failing file is reported at once. A document is identified in an error by its **position in the upload**, never by its file name — this component does not echo supplied values back. Duplicate file names on one claim are refused, uploads to a submitted claim are refused, and documents stay with the claim after it is submitted.

The servlet container's multipart limits sit deliberately above the policy (12 MB per file, 64 MB per request), so an oversized file reaches the policy check and the sponsor gets an error naming the document rather than a container-level failure. A sponsor attaching more than fits in one request uploads in several, up to the per-claim limit.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | Everything the claim now carries |
| `400` | A file that breaks the type, size or naming policy |
| `422` | The claim is already submitted, or this would exceed the per-claim limit |
| `404` | No such claim, or the `enableDocumentUpload` feature flag is off |

### Confirm the submission

`POST /api/claims/journey/{journeyId}/confirmation`

Completing the process issues the reference number the sponsor quotes, along with what it is for:

```json
{
  "referenceNumber": "DC-K7M2-9XPQ",
  "journeyId": "…",
  "policyNumber": "P100234",
  "memberId": "M0004821",
  "planId": "PLAN-LTD-01",
  "submittedAt": "2026-05-20T09:15:00Z",
  "documentCount": 2,
  "downloadPath": "/api/claims/journey/…/confirmation/download"
}
```

**The reference is issued once and then fixed.** A sponsor who reloads the page, posts again, or comes back next week finds the same number — otherwise the number proves nothing. It is drawn from an alphabet without `0`, `1`, `I`, `L` or `O` and grouped in fours, because a sponsor reads it down a telephone.

| Endpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/claims/journey/{journeyId}/confirmation` | Complete the process — issue the confirmation, or return the one already issued |
| `GET /api/claims/journey/{journeyId}/confirmation` | Show it again |
| `GET /api/claims/journey/{journeyId}/confirmation/download` | Take it away as a plain-text file (`Content-Disposition: attachment`) |

`referenceNumber` is a plain string so a copy button has nothing to strip out of it; the download endpoint is the other half of "copy or download".

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | The confirmation, on screen or as a file |
| `422` | The claim exists but has not been submitted yet |
| `404` | No such claim, no confirmation issued for it, or the `enableSubmissionConfirmation` flag is off |

### Check where a claim stands

`GET /api/claims/journey/{journeyId}/status`

```json
{
  "stage": "READY_TO_SUBMIT",
  "policyNumber": "P100234",
  "memberId": "M0004821",
  "planId": "PLAN-LTD-01",
  "referenceNumber": null,
  "submittedAt": null,
  "documentCount": 1,
  "missingFields": [],
  "outstandingItems": [
    { "code": "SUBMIT_CLAIM", "step": null, "description": "Submit the claim." },
    { "code": "CONFIRM_SUBMISSION", "step": null, "description": "Complete the process to receive the claim reference number." }
  ]
}
```

| Stage | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `DETAILS_OUTSTANDING` | Required employment or absence answers are still missing |
| `READY_TO_SUBMIT` | Everything required is answered; not submitted |
| `SUBMITTED` | Submitted, no reference number issued yet |
| `CONFIRMED` | Submitted and confirmed — the sponsor has a reference |

`outstandingItems` lists **everything** still to do, in the order it will be done, not just the next thing — someone returning to a half-finished claim is deciding whether they have ten minutes for it. Only genuine blockers appear: a claim with no documents is not outstanding, because nothing in the process requires one, so the status reports `documentCount` and leaves the judgement to the sponsor.

**Nothing here is stored.** The status is derived from the claim, its documents and its confirmation on every request, so it cannot fall behind the thing it describes — there is no status field anywhere in the codebase to go stale. `referenceNumber` and `submittedAt` are `null` until a confirmation is issued; the submission time is recorded with the reference (US-5), so it appears at `CONFIRMED` rather than at `SUBMITTED`.

Two outcomes only — `200` with the status, or `404` if there is no such claim or the `enableSubmissionStatus` flag is off. A claim that exists always has a status.

> **Known limitation.** Status is looked up by claim reference (`journeyId`). There is no "my claims" listing, because no store offers a query by policy or member — that needs a real datastore behind the existing seams, not another endpoint.

### Send the claim to intake

`POST /api/claims/journey/{journeyId}/packet/send`

A confirmed claim's information and its documents are packaged as one unit and handed across in a **single delivery**. Intake correlating a claim's details with its documents from separate messages is the failure this exists to remove, so the packet is assembled whole, digested whole, and sent whole.

| Endpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/claims/journey/{journeyId}/packet` | Describe what would be sent — details, document manifest, digests |
| `POST /api/claims/journey/{journeyId}/packet/send` | Send it to intake, once |
| `GET /api/claims/journey/{journeyId}/packet/delivery` | Whether it has been sent, and what intake acknowledged |

The packet carries a SHA-256 per document and a `contentDigest` over the claim reference, its details and those document digests. Intake can then say not merely that it received a file of the right name and size but that it received *this* file — which is what "associated" has to mean once a packet crosses a boundary. The digest covers content only, never the packet id, so the same claim always digests the same way and a resend is recognisable as the same packet rather than a second claim.

**A claim is never sent twice.** A duplicate packet is a duplicate claim in the insurer's systems, so the delivery ledger — not the caller — decides whether a send happens. A delivery that fails records nothing and can be retried.

The `GET /packet` endpoint describes documents by digest and size; it never renders their content. It exists so an operator can see what would be sent, not so a claim's files can be pulled back out through a second route.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | The packet, or the delivery intake acknowledged |
| `422` | The claim exists but has no reference number yet — confirm it first |
| `404` | No such claim, nothing sent for it, or the `enablePacketization` flag is off |
| `502` | The packet is sound and intake could not take it; nothing was recorded and it can be sent again |

> **There is no intake system yet.** `IntakeGateway` is the port; the shipped adapter records what it was handed rather than inventing a protocol nobody has agreed. The shape of the boundary is the deliverable — when a real intake exists, that one bean changes and nothing above it moves.
>
> Sending is also a deliberate action on this endpoint rather than something that fires automatically when a sponsor confirms. Wiring it to the confirmation would mean changing `submission-confirmation`, which belongs to another team; that is a follow-up ticket, not a wider diff.

### Feature flags

All seven ship **off**, so each endpoint returns `404` until a deployment opts in. Turning a flag off again is the rollback lever; removing the component code is the follow-up.
